chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Salih ibn 'Uqbah, from Abi Harun al-Makfuf, who said:
Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام said: O Aba Harun, the iqamah is part of the salat (prayer), so when you pronounce the iqamah, do not speak and do not gesture with your hand.

key_terms.الْإِقَامَةُ: the iqamah, the call immediately preceding the start of salat (prayer)
key_terms.يَا أَبَا هَارُونَ: O Aba Harun, the direct address of the Imam عليه السلام to the narrator

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام say about speaking during the iqamah?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that the iqamah is treated as part of the salat (prayer), and therefore it should be performed with attentiveness and restraint. It indicates a legal and devotional etiquette: one should avoid speaking or making hand gestures during the iqamah.
